analysis.title: Xcel Energy Inc. (XEL): First Take: EPS Beat vs. GSe and consensus, updated $70bn capital plan in focus
key_insights: XEL reported ongoing 3Q26 EPS of $1.52 versus GSe $1.40 and FactSet consensus $1.39. The variance against GS came mostly from higher earnings from equity method investments and slightly lower O&M expense.
By segment, NSPM ($0.51 vs $0.52 GSe), NSPW ($0.08 vs $0.09) and SPS ($0.34 vs $0.38) came in below GS estimates, PSCo was in line at $0.57, and Other was $0.01 vs a GSe of ($0.16), a $0.17 variance.
XEL narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to $4.10-$4.16 from $4.04-$4.16. GS forecasts $4.16, the top of the range.
XEL initiated 2027 EPS guidance of $4.48-$4.62 versus GSe $4.56, and formalized a 9+% EPS CAGR through 2031.
The updated base capital plan is $70bn. The company announced another $10bn+ of incremental investment opportunities from 15+ GW of additional generation needs and high-voltage transmission.
To fund the incremental capex, XEL raised its equity financing plan from $7bn to $8bn through 2031 and initiated a 2027 debt financing plan.
The data center pipeline appears unchanged. XEL disclosed customer protections including 75-80% minimum bills secured with parent guarantee and/or letter of credit.
GS wants more color on the call on the moving pieces in the earnings growth outlook. The company did not adjust guidance despite the higher capital plan, and GS numbers imply 10% growth through 2030.

GS expects the call to focus on pending rate cases and tariff filings, the capital and financing plan, wildfire mitigation and possible legislative reform next year, and RFP filings and transmission projects.

GS key call questions: how much of the capital plan upside serves data center growth, what is needed to convert the 20+ GW data-center pipeline into signed ESAs and reach the 2027 contracting target, and how the PUCT cost cap on SPS generation projects affects those investments.

market_movers.rationale: GS applies a 19.5x P/E to Q5-Q8 earnings, a 3x premium to its baseline multiple, for leverage to renewables and transmission, above-average growth versus peers and a strong execution record. Upside is 20.5% from $77.18.

earnings_insights: XEL ongoing 3Q26 EPS reported 10/29/2026: $1.52 ongoing vs GSe $1.40 and FactSet estimate $1.39.
3Q26 operating net income reported $961mn vs GSe $890mn (+8%). Other segment net income was $13mn vs GSe ($101mn).
2026 EPS guidance narrowed to $4.10-$4.16 (company guidance) from $4.04-$4.16. GSe is $4.16.
2027 EPS guidance initiated at $4.48-$4.62 (company guidance) vs GSe $4.56. GSe 2028E EPS is $5.03.

GS 3Q26 variance drivers: AFUDC equity $131mn vs GSe $117mn, other income $139mn vs GSe $20mn, AFUDC debt $52mn vs GSe $4mn. Total operating revenues were $4,172mn vs GSe $4,285mn, and income tax expense was $69mn vs GSe $18mn.
risk_factors: Failure to close the gap between earned and authorized ROE.
Wildfire exposure, with mitigation efforts and potential legislative reform next year on the call agenda.
Higher equity financing need, raised from $7bn to $8bn through 2031, against FCF yield of (16.0)% in 2026E per GS.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows 3Q26 EPS and net income by segment, GS estimate vs actual: NSPM $0.52 vs $0.51, PSCo $0.57 vs $0.57, NSPW $0.09 vs $0.08, SPS $0.38 vs $0.34, Other ($0.16) vs $0.01, XEL $1.40 vs $1.52.
Exhibit 2 shows the 3Q26 income statement variance: operating income $1,192mn vs GSe $1,236mn, total other income $270mn vs $136mn, and net income $961mn vs $890mn.
